title: Playing to inspire and building a solo
summary: Bobby Shew's advice and thoughts on shaping a solo against the previous soloist.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: I mean today, I mean a lot of it is technique. There’s so much technique involved in playing today. You know Bobby Shew once told me a great — you know Bobby Shew — he told me a great statement that I’ve always remembered. He said, “Do you play to impress or do you play to inspire?” And so I always think about that when I play. I’m not trying to dazzle you with my technique. I’m trying to like draw you into a theme, a melody, a theme, a set of changes in a direction that I’m going with my solo. So building the solo is important you know. I think you have to depend on who just soloed before you, because you have to keep that in your mind. If you have somebody playing hundreds of notes and a really busy solo, you can’t come in and keep doing that because it’s going © Fillius Jazz Archive -11-
to just be a continuation — and if you want people to listen to you basically you have to deflect the direction and go a different way to build your solo, to grab the listener.
